s.note: the radishes Peter pinches from Mr. McGregor's garden
s.how: Wash and trim 2 bunches radishes, leaving a little stem on, and halve the bigger ones. Keep in iced water for 15 minutes so they crunch. Whip 120g soft salted butter with an electric beater for 3 minutes until pale and fluffy. Spread the butter in a dish, sprinkle with sea salt flakes and snipped chives. Serve with the drained radishes and a warmed baguette.

s.n: Cottontail's garden crudités with herb dip
s.note: Peter, Benjamin and the girls raiding the garden
s.how: Trim 1 bunch baby carrots and 150g snow peas. Cut 1 Lebanese cucumber into batons and separate 2 baby cos lettuces into small leaves. Mix 250g Greek yoghurt with 1 small crushed garlic clove, 2 tbsp chopped dill, 1 tbsp chopped mint, the zest of 1 lemon and a pinch of salt. Arrange the vegetables around the bowl of dip on a big board.

m.note: Mr. McGregor's vegetable garden in the Lake District
m.how: Boil 500g diced potato and 2 diced carrots for 8 minutes and drain. Fry 2 sliced leeks in 40g butter for 6 minutes, stir in 3 tbsp plain flour, then whisk in 500ml milk and simmer until thick. Stir in 120g grated cheddar, 1 tsp Dijon, the vegetables and 150g peas. Tip into a pie dish, cover with 1 sheet puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.

w.note: Peter's blackberry attack on Thomas McGregor
w.how: Toss 500g blackberries, fresh or frozen, with 2 peeled diced apples, 60g caster sugar and 1 tbsp cornflour and tip into a baking dish. Rub 100g cold butter into 100g plain flour, then stir in 60g rolled oats and 80g brown sugar. Scatter over the fruit. Bake at 180C for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and bubbling. Serve warm with 600ml vanilla custard.

d.n: Mrs. Rabbit's chamomile apple iced tea
d.note: the chamomile tea from the Peter Rabbit stories
d.how: Steep 4 chamomile tea bags in 600ml boiling water with 2 tbsp honey for 5 minutes. Remove the bags and cool, then chill for 1 hour. Stir in 400ml cold apple juice and the juice of 1 lemon. Fill 4 glasses with ice and thin apple slices, pour over the tea and add a mint sprig to each.
